text:
Predicates:
Supervised(x) ::: x is supervised learning.
Unsupervised(x) ::: x is unsupervised learning.
Reinforcement(x) ::: x is reinforcement learning.
Labelled(x) ::: x requires labelled data.
Trained(x, y) ::: x is trained with y.
StateOfTheArt(x) ::: x is the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
Premises:
∃x (Supervised(x) ∨ Unsupervised(x) ∨ Reinforcement(x)) ::: Machine Learning algorithms can be categorized as supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning.
∀x (Unsupervised(x) → ¬Labelled(x)) ::: Unsupervised learning doesn't require labelled data.
∃x (Trained(stateOfTheArt, x)) ::: The state-of-the-art text summarization model is trained with machine learning algorithms.
¬∃x (Trained(stateOfTheArt, x) ∧ Reinforcement(x)) ::: Reinforcement learning is not used to train the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
∀x (Trained(stateOfTheArt, x) → Labelled(x)) ::: The Machine Learning algorithm for training text summarization model requires labelled data.
Conclusion:
∃x (Trained(stateOfTheArt, x) ∧ Unsupervised(x)) ::: Unsupervised learning is used to train the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
